# Mechanisms, Behaviour & Ethics
::: {.lead}
How rules shape outcomes, how people actually play, and what follows ethically: from auctions and matching to blockchains, experiments and historical cases.
:::
:::

## What you'll be able to do by the end

- Design mechanisms (VCG, matching, voting rules) and check whether they are incentive compatible.
- Work through revenue equivalence, Myerson's optimal auction, combinatorial auctions and GSP.
- Apply prospect theory, heuristics, nudges and time preferences to observed choices.
- Read and replicate classic laboratory and field experiments.
- Analyse blockchain incentives, MEV and DeFi protocols as games.
- Formalise ethical dilemmas and assess fairness in algorithmic and policy settings.
- Connect the theory to cases such as the Cold War, OPEC, climate negotiations and market design.

## Who should take this course

For readers who know Nash equilibrium and the canonical games from Course 1 and want to apply them to markets, institutions and behaviour.

## The other courses

- [Course 1 — Foundations of Game Theory](../course1-game-theory/index.qmd) — Equilibrium concepts and the canonical games, decisions under uncertainty, evolutionary, cooperative, behavioural and network games, and the history behind them.
- [Course 3 — Mathematical & Statistical Methods](../course3-methods/index.qmd) — Linear algebra, optimisation, information theory, statistics, Bayesian and causal inference, econometrics and network science: the toolkit behind the models.
- [Course 4 — Simulation, AI & Data Practice](../course4-simulation-ai-data/index.qmd) — Monte Carlo and agent-based simulation, machine learning and multi-agent AI, public data, visualisation, reproducible workflows and R packages.
